name: Wobbulator
description: CRT scan deflection modulator - displaces horizontal and vertical raster position
origin: Nam June Paik modified television sets by adding magnets and oscillators to deflection coils

behavior.summary: Modulates the X/Y position of scan lines creating warping, wobbling, and displacement effects
behavior.horizontal: H-rate modulation creates vertical bands of displacement
behavior.vertical: V-rate modulation creates horizontal bands of displacement
behavior.video_rate: Using video signal as modulator creates luminance-dependent warping

video_signal.description: Luminance of input video drives displacement
video_signal.effect: Bright areas push outward, dark areas pull inward (or inverse)

external_cv.description: Control voltage input for modular patching

parameters.video_mod_h: Video signal modulation of H displacement
parameters.video_mod_v: Video signal modulation of V displacement

transfer_function.equation_h: x' = x + amplitude_h * sin(2π * freq_h * y + phase_h) + video_mod_h * luminance(x,y)
transfer_function.equation_v: y' = y + amplitude_v * sin(2π * freq_v * x + phase_v) + video_mod_v * luminance(x,y)
transfer_function.notes: Original CRT wobbulator affected electromagnetic deflection coils

visual_effects: Feedback loops when output feeds modulation
historical_notes: Paik created first wobbulator by placing magnets on TV CRT
Abe refined technique with electronic oscillator modulation
Key to 'Global Groove' and other Paik video art pieces
Later refined by Rutt/Etra for Z-axis displacement
